## Natural history notes

A small earthstar fungus characterized by a round central spore sac surrounded by outer rays that split open and curl backward, giving it a star-like shape on the ground. In Florida, it is found in sandy soils, pine flatwoods, scrub, oak hammocks, lawns, and other dry to moderately moist habitats with leaf litter or organic debris. Like other earthstars, it releases spores from the central sac when struck by raindrops, wind, or disturbance, and the dried fruiting body may persist for some time after maturity.
